source: Sifrei Bamidbar 7:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 7:3; Sifrei Bamidbar 20:1; Onkelos Num 5:12; Onkelos Num 5:13; Onkelos Num 5:14
claim_en: THE SECTION'S PURPOSE: DOUBT AFTER WARNING AND SECRETING; WHO DRINKS. Deut 24:1 covers two witnesses (divorce); one witness, or DOUBT after the husband's warning and her secreting — this section: she drinks (row 7:1); 5:14's two arms in one verse ('and she is defiled... and she is not defiled' — computed) make the doubt the case (row 7:3); 'a man, a man' (the doubled man's four Torah seats, computed) includes the wife of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, one abroad or imprisoned — the COURT warns her, to void her marriage contract, not to make her drink; the widow awaiting the levir included, the betrothed excluded (R. Yoshiyah / R. Yonathan on which words — row 20:1); 'his wife' excludes forbidden unions; Akavya b. Mehalalel excludes the proselyte and the freed slave — the sages: Shemaya and Avtalyon gave Karkemit to drink; his coffin stoned (Mishnah Eduyot 5:6). Onkelos 'a man, a man, if his wife go astray and lie against him a lie'.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's purpose-row and its inclusions read as they stand; the two arms computed on the ink)

check.note: 'jealousy' — the spirit that opens the case

source: Onkelos Num 5:13; Sifrei Bamidbar 7:2; Sifrei Bamidbar 7:3
claim_en: THE SIX CONDITIONS, AND THE MINIMUM TIME'S SIX SETTINGS. 5:13 stacks six clauses — lain with, hidden from the husband, secreted, defiled, no witness against her, not seized — the last two alone in the Torah (computed); the Sifrei reads each: a man not a minor; 'with her' not her sister or any forbidden relation (the a-fortiori refused by the word); the husband not feigning blindness; witnesses to the SECRETING, none to the defiling; 'witness' = TWO unless 'one' is written (a paradigm from Deut 19:15); the forced excluded — but a priest's wife forbidden even forced; and THE MINIMUM TIME OF SECRETING — R. Yishmael (intercourse; circling a palm), R. Eliezer (pouring a cup), R. Yehoshua (drinking it), Ben Azzai (frying an egg), R. Akiva (swallowing it), R. Yehudah b. Beteira (three eggs) — six settings of one parameter (Mishnah Sotah 1:2; Sotah 4a). Onkelos 'no witness in her and she was not taken'.
middah: I3 (the paradigm for 'witness' = two; the six settings of the secreting's minimum recorded as a parameter)

check.note: '[she was not] seized' — the sixth condition, the Torah's one seat

claim_en: MERIT SUSPENDS THE WATERS — THE MIDDOT'S OWN CASE LAW ON THIS VERSE. 'An offering of memorial, a reminder of iniquity': R. Tarfon — the one memorial for punishment; R. Akiva — for merit too (5:28's seed); R. YISHMAEL — GENERAL-PARTICULAR: 'a reminder of sin' specifies the general 'memorial' — AND THE RULE: 'whenever a general-particular defeats an a-fortiori, if both can be satisfied the a-fortiori is not defeated' — so merit SUSPENDS: three months (Abba Yossi b. Chanan), nine (R. Eliezer b. Yitzchak), twelve (R. Yishmael), NOT AT ALL (R. Shimon b. Yochai — the deterrent diluted, the clean slandered); Rebbi: it suspends and she dies that death in the end; R. Shimon: her face turns green at once. A parameter with four settings (Mishnah Sotah 3:4-5). Onkelos 'a reminder of guilt'.
middah: I4 (general-particular on 'memorial' / 'reminder of sin', with the Sifrei's meta-rule on its meeting with the a-fortiori; the four settings recorded)

source: Onkelos Num 5:15; Onkelos Num 5:16; Onkelos Num 5:17; Sifrei Bamidbar 10:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 8:1
claim_en: THE EPHAH CONVERTED TO THREE SE'AH; THE LAVER NAMED; BARLEY MEAL; A NEW EARTHEN VESSEL. 'A tenth of the ephah of barley meal' (the plene spelling of the ephah here as at Exod 16:36, Num 28:5 against Leviticus' defective 5:11, 6:13 — computed) → Onkelos 'one of ten in THREE SE'AH of barley meal': the conversion layer on a DRY measure, after the shekel-to-sela (Menachot 77a); 'meal' at two Torah seats, Sarah's and this (computed); 'no oil, no frankincense' — Lev 5:11's sinner's-offering clause with 'pour' for 'put' (computed); R. Gamliel: a beast's deeds, a beast's food (row 8:1); 'holy water' (one seat) → Onkelos 'water of the LAVER', the Sifrei the same — water consecrated in a vessel, the laver's; 'an earthen vessel' (the vessel's six Torah seats, computed) — a NEW one by the identity with Lev 14:5's bird-vessel (R. Yishmael); the dust: the place consecrates; three things must be visible (row 10:1).
middah: I2 (the identity 'earthen vessel'/'earthen vessel' with Lev 14:5 for a new vessel; the conversion and the laver's name read as they stand)

check.note: 'the ephah' — plene, the measure Onkelos converts

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 9:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 11:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 12:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 13:1; Onkelos Num 5:16; Onkelos Num 5:17; Onkelos Num 5:18; Onkelos Num 5:19; Onkelos Num 5:20
claim_en: STOOD ALONE; THE HAIR UNCOVERED WITHIN LIMITS; THE PRIEST ADJURES IN ANY LANGUAGE AND OPENS FOR MERIT. Not two suspected wives together; not with her servants; at the Nicanor gate (row 9:1); 'uncover the woman's head' (the root's six Torah seats — the calf, the priests' heads, the leper, the high priest, the wife, the nazirite's locks — computed): from behind; R. Yishmael — from here the daughters of Israel cover their hair; R. Yehudah — what is becoming is not exposed; black garments, ornaments off; R. Yochanan b. Beroka — no more than the Torah prescribes; a sheet between him and the people (row 11:1; Mishnah Sotah 1:5-7); 'the priest shall adjure her' — she does not swear of herself; 'say to the woman' — in ANY language she understands (R. Yoshiyah; R. Yonathan from the two amens); HE OPENS FOR MERIT — 'if no man has lain with you' first (computed: the clean arm precedes the guilty at 5:19-20): much wine, much levity, do not let the Name be erased (row 12:1); the irregular mode and the impotent included (row 13:1). Onkelos 'be innocent'.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's procedure-rows read as they stand; the order of the oath's arms computed on the ink)

check.note: 'and [the priest] shall adjure' — the priest swears her

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 14:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 15:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 15:2; Onkelos Num 5:21; Onkelos Num 5:22
claim_en: OATH IS CURSE, UNDER THE NAME; AMEN, AMEN; THE SOTAH'S OATH IS THE PARADIGM FOR ALL OATHS. 'The oath of the curse' — Lev 5:1's 'curse' by the identity of wording: an oath is a curse there as here, and EVERY OATH IN THE TORAH is under the Name (5:21 'the LORD make you') — row 14:1 (the exam's Shevuot 35b-36a); 'amen, amen' — the bare doubled amen at two Tanakh seats, Num 5:22 and Neh 8:6 (computed; the Psalms' 'amen and amen' carry the conjunction): R. Meir — amen that I have not been, amen that I will not be (retroactive); the sages — amen on the oath, amen on the curse; for this man, for another; betrothed, married; awaiting the levir, after — the conditions must be of the married time (row 15:1; Mishnah Sotah 2:5); and from the one specified oath to ALL: with a curse, under the Name, answered amen — and the ROLLED oath (an earlier matter rolled onto the present) derived here for every oath, by an a-fortiori to thefts (row 15:2; Kiddushin 27b-28a). Onkelos keeps 'amen, amen'.
middah: I2 (the identity 'curse'/'curse' with Lev 5:1; the generalization from the one specified oath to all — the Sifrei's own form)

check.note: 'amen' — the first of the doubled pair

claim_en: THE SCROLL ERASED — THE ONE COMMAND TO ERASE WHAT IS WRITTEN IN HOLINESS. 'The priest shall write these curses in a scroll and erase into the bitter water' (the erasing verb's Torah seats: Deut 29:19 a sinner's NAME blotted, and this — computed; 34:11's 'and reach' the consonantal homograph): 'these' — not all the covenant's curses; 'the priest' — not any man (the identity with Deut 24:1's divorce-writ refused); on the erasable — a SCROLL of finished parchment, not a tablet, paper or hide; INK, not gum or vitriol (Mishnah Sotah 2:4); and the a-fortiori: if for peace between a man and his wife the Name written in holiness is erased, how much more the heretics' scrolls — R. Yishmael cuts out the Names, R. Akiva burns whole (Shabbat 116a). Onkelos 'in a scroll... and erase'.
middah: I1 (the Sifrei's a-fortiori from the Name's erasure to the heretics' scrolls; the material rules read as they stand)

check.note: 'and erase' — the command the Name obeys

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 17:1; Onkelos Num 5:24; Onkelos Num 5:25; Onkelos Num 5:26
claim_en: THE ORDER AND THE THREE CATEGORICAL REQUIREMENTS; WAVED — RENDERED LIFTED. The drinking written at 5:24 and again at 5:26-27: R. Akiva — after the erasure she is forced if she refuses; R. Shimon — THREE THINGS ARE CATEGORICAL: the scroll's erasure, the fistful's offering, her acceptance of the oath; erased, then 'I am unclean' — the water spilled, the offering scattered, the scroll invalid for another (R. Achi b. R. Yoshiyah: valid) — Mishnah Sotah 3:3; the ORDER written in the ink: the fistful burned, THEN she drinks (5:26 'and after' — computed); 'from the woman's hand' — not her agent; 'wave': back and forth AND up and down — lifting likened to waving by Exod 29:27 (rows 17:1, 37:1); Onkelos renders the waving verb by the LIFTING verb here and at 6:20 — one Aramaic verb for the Hebrew two; the fistful's 'memorial' is Lev 2:2's word.
middah: plain (the Sifrei's requirements and order read as they stand; the rendering computed on the shelf's bytes)

check.note: 'and after' — the fistful before the drink

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 15:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 18:1; Onkelos Num 5:21; Onkelos Num 5:22; Onkelos Num 5:23; Onkelos Num 5:24; Onkelos Num 5:25; Onkelos Num 5:26; Onkelos Num 5:27
claim_en: THIGH FIRST, BELLY FIRST — FROM THE LIMB WHERE THE SIN BEGAN. The ink writes 'your thigh falling and your belly swelling' at 5:21 (thigh first) and 'to swell belly and make thigh fall' at 5:22, 'her belly shall swell and her thigh fall' at 5:27 (belly first) — computed; R. Yossi HaGelili reads 5:22's reversal as the ADULTERER'S limbs (5:21 already the adulteress's) — punishment overtakes him too, and by an a-fortiori the stronger attribute of good (row 15:1); and on 5:27: belly and thigh NAMED because FROM THE LIMB WHENCE THE SIN BEGAN THE PUNISHMENT BEGINS — the flood, Sodom, Pharaoh, the condemned city (row 18:1) — a pattern on the punishment's FORM with five scriptural seats; 'a curse in the midst of her people' — they curse and swear by her (Isa 65:15). Onkelos 'thigh wasting, bowels swollen'.
middah: E7 (the pattern read across seats — the limb-order as the form of the punishment; the orders computed on the ink; R. Yossi HaGelili's a-fortiori recorded)

claim_en: WHO DEFILED HER THAT SCRIPTURE MUST CLEANSE HER? SOWN WITH SEED — THE TRANSLATION TAKES THE REFUTED ARM. Lev 20:10: witnesses and warning → death; witnesses without warning → forbidden to her husband (Deut 24:1); DOUBT → this verse: since an evil name went out against her she is forbidden until she drinks; 'clean' — to her husband, to the cohabitor, to the heave-offering; 'absolved' — of the curses and the oath; 'she shall be sown with seed' (the clause's one seat, computed): R. Yishmael — if barren, she conceives; R. AKIVA — then every barren woman will secrete herself to conceive — rather, females become males, one becomes two, dark fair, short tall; R. Shimon — no reward for transgression: she was forbidden for seed and is permitted; variantly the wombless excluded from drinking. Onkelos 'she shall go out innocent and shall CONCEIVE a conception' — R. Yishmael's arm in the translation, R. Akiva's objection on the shelf beside it: RECORDED. The row's head is mistyped in the export ('5:298'), placed by position (RESEARCH_LOG.md).
middah: plain (the Sifrei's row read as it stands; the translation's arm and the objection recorded together, neither chosen)

check.note: 'and she shall be sown' — the disputed promise

source: Sifrei Bamidbar 20:1; Sifrei Bamidbar 21:1; Onkelos Num 5:29; Onkelos Num 5:30; Onkelos Num 5:31
claim_en: THIS IS THE LAW — THE FIRST OF THREE; OBLIGATORY; THE WATERS TEST ONLY A CLEAN HUSBAND. 'This is the law of jealousies' — the formula's first of three in the portion (5:29, 6:13, 6:21 — computed): R. Yoshiyah, for the generations; R. Yonathan, a summation (the same pair on each — rows 20:1, 32:1, 38:1); 'or a man' (5:30, the jealousy-spirit's second seat, computed) — the drinking OBLIGATORY, not optional (row 21:1); 'the man shall be clean of iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity' (the last clause's one seat, computed): if he did so; he should not say 'I killed a daughter of Israel'; Shimon b. Azzai — the clean woman who secreted herself does not escape; and by HOSEA 4:14 — when the men are clean, the waters test the wives; if the husbands pursue harlotry the waters do not test (Mishnah Sotah 9:9's abolition; Sotah 47b): a gate on the ordeal in the husband's own field. Onkelos 'the woman shall RECEIVE her sin'; the defilement-root's eight tokens in the section counted (the one with the conjunction at 5:29 — R. Akiva's three on the shelf).
middah: plain (the Sifrei's rows read as they stand; the formulas and the root-count computed on the ink)
